subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Maxwell's First Equation: Gauss for Electricity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Maxwell's First Equation: Gauss for Electricity.

hook.text: Maxwell took four equations and unified all of electromagnetism. The first is Gauss's law.

buildup.text: Electric flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by ε₀.

discovery.text: Charges are sources of electric field lines — they start and end on charges.

twist.text: In a region with no charge, field lines can pass through but never originate.

climax.text: This single equation explains Coulomb's law, shielding, and conductor behavior.

punchline.text: Charge is where electric field lines are born and where they die.

quiz.question: What does Maxwell's first equation tell us about electric field lines?
options: They form closed loops with no beginning or end
They originate and terminate on electric charges
They are always parallel to magnetic field lines
